message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for Marvin Gardens.

I have $889 cash and the current bid is $120. A $121 bid would mortgage Marvin Gardens for $140 and net me cash. I am weighing whether to push toward my $170 ceiling or fade near $139.

A $121 bid would net me $19 cash after mortgaging the property. I cannot build on it while it is mortgaged.

I already own Atlantic Avenue, so I cannot complete the yellow monopoly even if I buy Marvin unmortgaged. The strategic value is blocking p1 from a cheap flip and creating a trade target with p4 for Ventnor. p1 has $320 cash but his red monopoly is broken because Kentucky and Indiana are mortgaged.

p1 can also mortgage the property for $140, so the flip is profitable for them until $139. They have less cash cushion because their orange properties are dangerous and they are in jail. I should continue bidding $121 since I am still safely below the $140 mortgage floor. p1 may be trying to force me to pay more or deny me the two-thirds yellow set.

I am calculating rent values to preserve cash for future landings. New York Avenue with three houses costs $600, and Virginia Avenue with three houses is another major expense.

Virginia Avenue with three houses costs $500. p4 has hotels on Mediterranean and Baltic, plus three railroads and a light blue house. He owns Ventnor, North Carolina Avenue, and Pennsylvania Avenue, completing a two-thirds green set.

I have a full unmortgaged dark blue monopoly on Park Place and Boardwalk. I am calculating the $200 house cost to build evenly, noting that Boardwalk rent rises to $1700 with four houses.

I will bid $121 and continue one-dollar increments. I am not building on the dark blue set now; that is a separate decision.

I am reconsidering the $170 ceiling. If p1 and I value the property similarly, a dollar auction can overpay slightly. My edge is having more cash and owning the two-thirds yellow set, which gives me stronger strategic leverage than p1, who has no yellows. I should be willing to bid above $140 because of the monopoly potential.
